title: Bitcoin and ether recover as stablecoin rules advance and portfolio value rises
paragraphs: Bitcoin rose 2.4% over 24 hours to about $83,400, while ether gained 3.5% to $2,467. The broader picture was mixed: CoinGecko's total crypto market capitalization slipped 0.3% to $2.81 trillion. The recovery in the two largest assets therefore does not describe the whole market.

UK inflation added pressure to the interest-rate outlook. Annual consumer-price inflation accelerated to 3.5% from 3.1%, with motor fuels the biggest contributor to the increase. Core inflation including housing also rose. For crypto, persistent inflation is a risk because it can keep borrowing costs elevated and constrain demand for speculative assets.

The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued its final GENIUS Act rule, setting requirements for payment-stablecoin issuers and certain custody activities under its supervision. The framework covers reserve backing, redemption and risk management. It takes effect January 18, 2027; anti-money-laundering and sanctions rules will follow separately, and the agency has yet to announce when applications open. Issuers now have a clearer operational framework, though implementation still has several steps ahead.

Mastercard opened developer early access to Agent Pay for Machines after pilots involving Coinbase, Base, Cloudflare and other partners. Businesses assign agents spending limits, and agents use signed vouchers to purchase digital services, with settlement handled later. A demonstration used Coinbase wallet infrastructure and Base settlement. This gives developers a concrete way to test payments for data, computing and AI services within approved budgets. Early access is a testing milestone, with commercial adoption still to be demonstrated.

Bitwise's newly released staking report shows Ethereum finished the third quarter with 43.8 million ETH staked, or 35.9% of supply. Its average staking yield fell to 2.63% from 2.81% as participation grew. Solana's tokenized-equity volume rose 45% to $6.93 billion. These quarterly figures show expanding participation and financial applications, alongside lower rewards per staked token. More activity does not automatically translate into a higher yield for holders.

Our on-chain portfolio is about $78,600: $11,600 in the active treasury and $67,000 in the cold-storage Safe. Its marked value increased $2,758, or 3.6%, from the previous verified edition. The Safe still holds 26.74 million ARC directly, unchanged in quantity and worth about $52,758, up $1,785. That single holding represents 67% of the total. Its $10,859 WETH/ARC pool adds further ARC exposure, leaving concentration the dominant portfolio risk.

The treasury has roughly $3,572 in Beefy pools and $2,566 in cbETH. Combined net Aave value rose about $285 to $5,295; treasury and Safe health factors improved from 2.46 to 2.54 and from 1.96 to 2.03. Visible lending debt totals about $4,197. Fluid remains the tightest lending position: $1,213 supplied, $1,060 borrowed and a 1.03 health factor, a narrow liquidation cushion despite its small $153 net value.
